questions.q:

4. Notochord is a mesodermally derived rod-like structure formed on the ventral side during embryonic development in some animals.
5. The body cavity, which is lined by mesoderm is called acoelom
questions.solution: In sponges, the cells are arranged as loose cell aggregates, i.e., they exhibit cellular level of organisation. ,Presence or absence of a cavity between the body wall and the gut wall is very important in classification. The body cavity, which is lined by mesoderm is called coelom. Animals possessing coelom are called coelomates, e.g., annelids, molluscs, arthropods, echinoderms, hemichordates and chordate

questions.solution: The forelimbs in aves are modified into wings. The hind limbs generally have scales and are modified for walking, swimming or clasping the tree branches.They are warm-blooded (homoiothermous) animals, i.e.,they are able to maintain a constant body temperature.

questions.q:
Levels of organizationDescription
A. Cellular Level1. Cells performing the same function are grouped into tissues.
B. Tissue Level2. Tissues are grouped together to form organs with specific functions.
C. Organ Level3. Organs form functional systems for physiological processes.
D. Organ System Level4. Cells are arranged as loose aggregates with some division of labor.
questions.solution: The cellular level involves loose cell aggregates (A - 4). The tissue level involves cells organized into tissues (B - 1). The organ level involves tissues forming organs (C - 2). The organ system level involves organs forming functional systems (D - 3).
